messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager — CI pipeline job build-main #842 failed artifact verification and pushed an artifact with mismatched build metadata. Failing post-publish hook. Link: https://ci.redwood.internal/builds/842 — root ts 1768402025

maria g: Paging oncall — canaries were live for the 22:50 roll. Anyone seeing customer impact?

raj p: Yep canaries were at ~4% traffic. I'm looking at registry and runner logs now.

maria g: Edge alerts show spike of 502s for /v1/chat/completions around 22:53. Not huge but burning SLO.

raj p: Quick find: registry entry for image sha:sha1234 has label `release_channel` set to "staging" but pipeline declared "canary". That mismatch can cause our rollout selector to route incorrectly.

raj p: Dump from registry API:
```
curl -s https://registry.internal/v2/redwood/inference/manifests/sha1234 | jq '.config.labels'
{
  "build_id": "842",
  "release_channel": "staging",
  "git_ref": "main"
}
```

arthur: That explains the partial traffic to an older variant -> 502s and 5xx tail latency.

maria g: Do we have customer-facing errors? Any enterprise tenants hit?

jen li: Support here — two enterprise tenants in the canary cohort reported elevated latencies and occasional 502s. I'm opening cases.

raj p: Root cause hypothesis: CI step `artifact-meta-sync` reused a warmed cache layer and accidentally copied labels from the cached artifact. When the post-publish validation is skipped the wrong label goes out.

arthur: Mitigation plan: 1) pause canary traffic (flip rollout kill-switch) 2) remove the bad artifact alias so it won't be selected 3) kick a rollback for canary deployment 4) patch CI to validate labels pre-publish.

maria g: I'm toggling the canary flag now. @deploy-bot can you remove the canary alias for sha1234?

deploy-bot: @maria g acknowledged. Removing canary alias for image sha1234... done — alias removed, propagation ~30s.

deploy-bot: Triggering rollback: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/inference-canary --to-revision=4` — started.

raj p: Running a scan across recent artifacts to quantify scope. Posting results in 2m.

raj p: Scan result: 6 artifacts in last 72h had `release_channel` not matching the pipeline-declared channel. Looks like cache path hit and wrote stale labels.

arthur: Customer impact note: three enterprise customers in canary experienced 5-10s tail latency and retries; no data loss, no PII exposure. Support notified and cases created.

jen li: I'll send CS template: apology, ETA for fix, and mitigation taken. Case IDs will be posted to the incident ticket.

maria g: Handing off — I have a hard stop in ~25m. @jen li can you take oncall for the next 2 hours? I'll remain reachable for questions.

jen li: Taking the handoff. Please post rollback completion and CI PR link.

deploy-bot: Rollback completed. `deployment/inference-canary` is at revision 4. Health checks are green.

raj p: Created PR 998 with a quick-fix: pre-publish label verification + unit test for cache reuse path. Will run a gated smoke and request review.

maria g: What followups for the postmortem?

arthur: Action items: - Raj: patch CI & add integration test (ETA 24h) - DevInfra: registry push guard to reject mismatched pipeline metadata (ETA 48h) - Support: customer outreach + RCA blurb (ETA 6h) - Ops: add a monitor for label drift against declared pipeline channel (ETA 72h)

maria g: Created Jira tasks and assigned owners. Thanks folks. :thumbsup:

jen li: Posting a short summary to #incidents and updating the external status page.

prod-monitor-bot: SLO graph shows metrics returned to baseline after rollback and flag toggle.

maria g: Offcall now. @jen li you own the incident. Ping me if blocker emerges.
